events.credibility_reason: Retitled from 'A complete proof' to 'A counting argument' without stated reason; only endorsements are from the author's advisors; one unverified read reports Remark 1.6 makes Section 4 depend on the Green–Griffiths–Lang conjecture for finite covers of abelian varieties.

why: The statement concerns rational points on varieties over number fields and their field extensions. The geometric (function fields over C, characteristic 0) results of Xie–Yuan and Gao are a separately named analogue: C(B) is not a finitely generated extension of a number field, and the geometric conjecture is a different question. So they are variants, which settles the close call against the record's competing reading. Gao's claim would be a variant even on the broader reading's best day, and it is also doubtful. Bresciani gives a reduction (none). Balakrishnan–Caro determine W2(Q) for selected curves where finiteness is already known (Faltings), so this is finitely many instances. The surveys are none. The Campana paper is about integral points and orbifold Mordell, so it is a variant. The Xie survey's AI assistant helped with writing only, so its role is none.
doubts: If 'field extensions' were read to include function fields over C, Gao 2025 would be a case-level claim (unreviewed, doubtful) and Xie–Yuan would be pre-snapshot cases. I answered on the statement's naming of number fields.
